title: How long different tissues take to fully renew themselves

source.name: Cell turnover rate research (Karolinska Institute / cell biology literature)
source.publisher: Peer-reviewed cell biology studies, as compiled by Scientific American and standard cell-biology references

notes: Stomach lining epithelial cells renew every 2-9 days (using ~5 as a midpoint); skin's outer layer renews roughly every 2-4 weeks (~28 days); red blood cells live about 120 days; the human skeleton is fully remodeled roughly every 10 years (~3,650 days). Figures are commonly cited ranges/midpoints, not exact for every individual.
